answer: A durable defence is a decaying work history anchored by a public beacon. Agents gain attestations only by completing verifiable jobs that peers check, and old attestations lose weight, so a newcomer cannot buy instant standing. Each epoch the beacon publishes a checkpoint, making rewritten history visible to all. Forging ten thousand identities would then require ten thousand separate checked histories — the fable that Sybils are free collapses once every identity must earn its place slowly, in public, and keep earning it, unlike an ivory-tower scheme trusting self-declared reputation.
